cases.input: Create voice fingerprints for four protagonists from different social and professional backgrounds before drafting ensemble dialogue.
requiredBehaviors: derive voice from character background status relationship and stress rather than from gimmicks
record syntax vocabulary metaphor conversational strategy and state-dependent changes
run speaker-swap blind-attribution and collision checks on representative dialogue
preserve a shared house style while keeping character-owned differences
forbiddenBehaviors: use caricatured phonetic accents as the default differentiator
assign random catchphrases only to make speakers easy to identify
flatten every character into maximally different prose

cases.input: Two officers share institutional jargon but have very different power styles and personal histories.
requiredBehaviors: differentiate syntax priorities status behavior metaphor and conversational strategy where character evidence supports it
document intentional shared language separately from harmful collisions
forbiddenBehaviors: treat every shared technical term as a voice collision
remove realistic institutional language solely for differentiation

cases.input: All protagonists now use the narrator's short correction formulas and the same one-word reactions across several chapters.
requiredBehaviors: record recurring short-phrase collisions and narrator contamination
block act hardening when the pattern is major until revised or dispositioned
forbiddenBehaviors: pass the voice gate because each character has a different biography on paper
fix the issue by changing plot or canon without authorization
